currentContext.expansion: Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private Limited (ARCS), a wholly owned subsidiary, is establishing a battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu. Battery Breaker operations commenced during the year and are in ramp-up. Refining operations, which started in H2 2024, continue to scale up. Phase II refinery expansion is underway with commissioning targeted by 2027. Commissioning of the Crystallizer and De-sulphurisation plant is expected shortly. Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited (ARACT) is progressing its lithium-ion cell and battery pack manufacturing capabilities. The Pack Assembly Plant is ramping up towards a targeted annual supply capacity of 1.5 GWh. The Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) with cylindrical and prismatic cell manufacturing lines is in the process of commissioning. Construction at the Amara Raja Giga Corridor in Divitipally, Telangana, progressed substantially, with structural development and procurement of key process equipment advancing. Start of Production (SoP) for lithium-ion cell manufacturing is planned for 2027.

risks.risk: Execution risk in scaling new lithium-ion cell manufacturing
risks.note: ARACT is in early-stage ramp-up with net losses, targeting Start of Production by 2027; delays or cost overruns at the Giga Corridor could impact the strategic pivot to New Energy.

Shift from lead-acid to lithium-ion and advanced chemistries (LFP, NMC) exposes the company to technology risk, customer qualification delays, and potential stranded assets in legacy battery segments.

risks.risk: Raw material supply and circular-economy integration
risks.note: ARCS recycling ramp-up (Phase II refinery, de-sulphurisation) is critical for lead and alloy security. Delays in scaling refining or alloy production could disrupt cost and supply-chain resilience.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk in battery waste management
risks.note: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, and evolving environmental norms require continuous investment and operational adaptation, especially for recycling and lead operations.
Automotive and industrial battery segments rely on a concentrated OEM customer base; shifts in OEM procurement strategies or EV adoption rates could materially affect volumes and margins.
Increasing digitalisation across manufacturing, R&D, and customer interfaces elevates exposure to cyber threats, which could disrupt operations or compromise sensitive data.

The company is exposed to tightening climate regulations, carbon pricing, and investor expectations. Failure to meet SBTi or GHG reduction targets could lead to reputational damage and higher cost of capital.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited is an Indian energy and mobility solutions provider with a strong legacy in lead-acid batteries, now diversifying into lithium-ion cells, battery packs, energy storage, and recycling.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ARE&M manufactures automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries under brands like Amaron and Quanta, and is expanding into new energy through lithium-ion cell and pack manufacturing, EV charging, and battery recycling. The company serves OEMs, aftermarket customers, and infrastructure developers across over 70 countries, with a growing focus on energy storage systems and advanced cell technologies.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Amara Raja Batteries Middle East (FZE) — subsidiary: Incorporated in Sharjah, UAE on July 31, 2018
- Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: Incorporated on June 2, 2022
- Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Incorporated on November 29, 2022
- Amara Raja Power Systems Limited — subsidiary: Acquired on September 29, 2023

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Lead Acid (92% rev): 4W OEM +30%, Aftermarket +5-6%, Tubular +35% (70-75% in-house); New Energy (8% rev): INR 280cr, 300MWh telecom packs supplied, 1GWh cumulative installed.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Automotive Batteries:** AMARON
- **Industrial Batteries:** Quanta (UPS), PowerZone
- **New Energy Batteries:** Lithium-ion battery packs, EV charging solutions, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Home Energy systems (Home UPS/HUPS)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: No formal backlog disclosed; BESS strategy relies on self-offtake and anticipated government localization mandates rather than binding long-term contracts.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 Revenue: Mid-to-high single digit (Lead Acid); Margin: Targeting 13-14% long-term (currently 11-12%); Order Inflow: Strong telecom/ESS pipeline; Capex: INR 1,500-1,700cr (INR 1,100-1,200cr New Energy).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 16-20GWh cell capacity target; 5-10GWh ESS integration facility by end-CY26; Expansion into 4W OEM lithium programs; Auxiliary battery demand in hybrids.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Raw material pressure: Lead/Alloys (70% basket) up due to geopolitics; Plastics (10% basket) +40% potential increase; Price hike of 5-6% taken in Q4, another 2-3% expected; Recycling accretion ~0.5%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: INR 100cr infused into AR Advanced Cell Technologies in Q4 (total INR 1,500cr invested); Focus on R&D lab commissioning and pilot line stabilization.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established brand leadership in lead-acid batteries with strong distribution network across India and presence in 70+ countries.
- Vertically integrated operations through subsidiary ARCS for battery recycling, securing lead and alloy supply.
- Diversifying into new energy with integrated platform spanning cell manufacturing, pack assembly, energy storage, and EV charging.
- Long-standing technology partnerships and in-house R&D for advanced lead-acid and lithium-ion technologies.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Chinese technology licensing restrictions (Gotion deal stalled); Import cost disadvantage (China +15-20%); Lead price volatility; Slower EV adoption if localization mandates raise system costs.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly states they will not be cost-competitive with Chinese imports initially (15-20% gap), betting entirely on government localization mandates (ALMM-style) for utility BESS to bridge the gap; Shift from EV-centric to ESS-centric near-term growth.
